HUGE PIECE IN THE TIMES TODAY!

I am delighted to see the @thetimes cover my thoughts on health in such a big way today.

We are an over-medicated country. 80-90% of what doctors see each day is in some way related to our collective modern lifestyles - yet, most of the options you get given by your doctor relate to pharmaceutical medication.

WE WILL NOT OUT-PRESCRIBE OUR WAY OUT OF THE CURRENT HEALTHCARE CRISIS - THERE HAS TO BE (AND THERE IS!!) ANOTHER WAY.

The number of prescriptions that we give out as doctors has increased by over 80 per cent in the last 20 years. And the uncomfortable truth is that a lot of the pills are simply not working.

This Thursday on @channel4 at 8pm my new 1 hour prime time documentary ‘Live Well With The Drug Free Doctor’ comes out. It is a deep dive into the healthcare crisis and I show how in 3 different conditions, type 2 diabetes, chronic pain & depression, it is possibly to completely heal without the use of medication.

Our lifestyles can be our very best medicine. That is what my entire public facing career is all about and I cannot wait for the British public to watch the Channel 4 show this Thursday evening at 8pm.

Let me know your thoughts below and if you plan on watching this Thursday, drop me a ❤️ below!

❤️ A SPECIAL MOMENT
My mum is an absolute legend and it’s always a special moment to show her a finished copy of one of my books - this time, the new version of ‘Happy Mind, Happy Life’.

My dad died in 2013 so never got to see a single one of my books. And, there have been times over the past few years when I didn’t think she’d be around to see the publication of any more.

It really is a special moment to show your parents something that you have worked on for so long - especially, when they have been such a positive influence on your life. Mum (and Dad) have brought me up really well and have always taught me and showed me the importance of treating every single person with kindness and respect - and this, in turn, is something I try my best to teach my own kids.

One thing I always appreciate about my mum is how honest and direct she is with me - she never sugarcoats what she thinks and I wouldn’t want it any other way!!

Just a few days now until this version of the book is on the shelves - if you’re planning on buying it for yourself or someone in your life, let me know below!

Canada, what a wonderful few days🇨🇦

I’ve had such a special time bringing my Thrive Tour to Toronto and Vancouver. Meeting so many of you in person, hearing your stories, answering your questions and feeling the energy in both rooms is something I’ll remember for a long time.

I’m feeling incredibly grateful to everyone who came along and made both evenings what they were. AND I managed to explore a little of two beautiful cities along the way.

Where in Canada should I visit next time? Let me know below 👇🏾

For now, I’m heading home before the Thrive Tour continues in Europe in just over a month. I can’t wait to see some of you there:

Dr Tommy Wood is BACK ON MY PODCAST (for his fifth appearance!). Every time we speak, he gives me something new to think about. Today, one of those big questions is this:

How do you actually feel about getting older? It’s a question worth sitting with.

I think we often focus on what we eat, how much we exercise and how well we sleep, but perhaps we don’t pay enough attention to how we actually think about ageing.

Of course, studies like this are complex, and we can’t simply say that thinking positively will make you live longer. But we do know that our mindset can influence how we engage with the world, the choices we make and even aspects of our physiology.

Dr Tommy Wood is Assistant Professor of Paediatrics and Neuroscience at the University of Washington, and this is his fifth appearance on my podcast. Every time we speak, he gives me something new to think about.

In this week’s latest episode of my ‘Feel Better, Live More’ podcast, Tommy and I tackle the seven biggest mistakes people make when it comes to protecting their brain as they get older — and the practical steps to address every one of them. Tune in to episode 681 to hear more 🎧
What’s one thing you’re grateful for today? I’d love to hear it 👇🏾

WHY do you want to live longer? It’s worth asking yourself honestly.

That question sits at the heart of this conversation with brain health expert @drtommywood . And today, we tackle the biggest mistakes people make when it comes to protecting their brain and longevity.

You can solo optimise. You can track every biomarker, take every supplement, follow every protocol. But if you lose your connection to other people in the pursuit of living longer, you may never actually get the thing you were trying to live longer for in the first place.

In this week’s NEW episode of my ‘Feel Better, Live More’ podcast, Tommy and I cover seven common brain health mistakes and the practical steps to address every one of them, including why focusing on solo health habits at the expense of social connection is something we should avoid if we can. Do you think of stress as something to avoid at all costs?

We hear so much about reducing stress, but stress itself isn’t necessarily the problem. In fact, as Dr Tommy Wood explains, stress is one of the ways our body knows it needs to adapt.

reading.signal: Mission statement: 'His mission is to help 100 million people around the globe live better lives.'
reading.inference: Thinks at enormous scale and is driven by purpose rather than just status. A partner would need to share or at least respect a life organised around a big mission, with the time and energy demands that brings.

reading.signal: Left hospital medicine (Internal Medicine Physician, NHS, 2001–2008) and moved into BBC TV, a podcast founded in 2018, books and documentaries
reading.inference: Took the risk of leaving a conventional medical path to build something of his own. Entrepreneurial and willing to bet on his convictions. He likely values a partner who backs bold moves.

reading.signal: Repeated posts on couples therapist Terrence Real: 'Do the people you love get the best of you – or what's left of you?' and learning to 'come home and open your heart, even when you're tired'
reading.inference: Reflective about the work that intimacy takes. He is probably emotionally articulate and would appreciate a partner who talks openly about connection and doesn't let busy lives crowd out the relationship.

reading.signal: Four pillars 'Relax, Eat, Move, Sleep'; his first book is 'where everything began for me… the foundation of everything I do'
reading.inference: Likely lives by simple, consistent routines around food, movement, rest and sleep. A compatible partner would enjoy home cooking, walks and early nights more than late-night chaos.

reading.signal: 'Health is not about chasing the latest trends or fads. It's about getting the basics right'; known for his 'ability to simplify complex health advice'
reading.inference: Values clarity and substance over hype. He probably appreciates straightforward, unpretentious conversation and a partner who is grounded rather than trend-driven.

reading.signal: Shares ideas from Buddhist monks Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and Gelong Thubten on embracing boredom, gratitude and learning 'to be with yourself' instead of scrolling
reading.inference: Drawn to contemplative ideas about presence and inner calm. A good date might be slow and phone-free, with a conversation about what makes people content.

reading.signal: Featured expert on 'Swiped: The School That Banned Smartphones'; says he has 'seen the impact of technology on mental and emotional health'
reading.inference: Probably intentional about screen time. He would value a partner who can put the phone away and be fully present.

reading.signal: Sat down with 'my good friend Dr Tommy Wood for the 5th time (a record for the podcast!)'
reading.inference: Builds long-term, loyal relationships and blends friendship with his work. He enjoys returning to deep conversations with the same people over years, which points to someone who values depth over novelty.

reading.signal: Hosts 'Feel Better, Live More', which he says reaches 8 million people monthly; regular BBC Breakfast and Radio 4 contributor
reading.inference: A natural communicator and curious interviewer who is comfortable in public life. A partner should be at ease with a high-profile life and a schedule shaped by recording, publishing and media work.

reading.signal: Squash Team at The University of Edinburgh
reading.inference: A competitive racquet sport from his student days hints at a sporty, energetic side. An active date, such as a game or a hike, might suit him.

reading.signal: Languages: Bengali, English, French
reading.inference: Multilingual. He may enjoy travel, other cultures, or a partner who shares a love of language.

reading.signal: Grew up at The Manchester Grammar School (1988–1995) and is still based in Greater Manchester
reading.inference: Rooted in his home region despite a national profile. Home and place likely matter to him, and a partner open to a Manchester-based life would fit well.

reading.signal: 'Cooking with a new ingredient' highlighted as one of the gems of wisdom he shared
reading.inference: Enjoys small, everyday experiments in the kitchen. Cooking together would be a natural shared activity.

reading.signal: Asks followers 'what would you like to focus on in the month ahead?'; latest book is 'Make Change That Lasts'
reading.inference: Oriented toward reflection, intention-setting and growth. He would connect with a partner who is also working on themselves and enjoys talking about goals.

reading.signal: 'It's a real full-circle moment for me' about republishing his first book ten years on
reading.inference: Sentimental about origins and milestones. He likely celebrates meaningful moments and appreciates a partner who notices how far someone has come.

reading.signal: Co-created the Royal College of GPs accredited 'Prescribing Lifestyle Course' and is Professor of Health Communication and Education at the University of Chester
reading.inference: A teacher at heart who gets satisfaction from equipping others. He is likely generous with knowledge, though a partner may need to signal when they want support rather than advice.

reading.signal: Post 3: showing his mum a finished copy of 'Happy Mind, Happy Life' — 'My mum is an absolute legend… My dad died in 2013 so never got to see a single one of my books.' Photo shows him reading the book aloud beside her at a kitchen table.
reading.inference: Deeply family-rooted and openly sentimental; a big part of his drive seems to be making his parents proud. He's comfortable showing grief and tenderness publicly — a partner should expect his mum to be central in his life.

reading.signal: Video caption: 'In 1962 my Dad travelled from India to Britain'
reading.inference: He carries his family's story with him and frames his own life against his parents' sacrifices; gratitude and legacy are core themes for him.

reading.signal: The Times piece and his caption: 'WE WILL NOT OUT-PRESCRIBE OUR WAY OUT OF THE CURRENT HEALTHCARE CRISIS - THERE HAS TO BE (AND THERE IS!!) ANOTHER WAY.' Article notes he stopped practising as a GP in March 2024 after 23 years.
reading.inference: Conviction-driven and willing to take a contrarian public stance; he walked away from a long, secure clinical career to pursue a mission. High risk appetite when it's in service of what he believes.

reading.signal: Post 9: 'You can solo optimise… But if you lose your connection to other people in the pursuit of living longer, you may never actually get the thing you were trying to live longer for.'
reading.inference: For all the health talk, he prizes connection over biohacking. He'd value a partner who prioritises time together and relationships over rigid routines.

reading.signal: Photo: writing in a notebook in a yellow armchair — 'Asking myself these 3 questions every morning has changed my life'
reading.inference: Reflective, structured morning person with a journaling habit. Likely appreciates quiet, intentional mornings and introspective conversation.

reading.inference: Busy touring schedule means lots of travel; he squeezes in exploring and is curious about new places. A partner would need to be comfortable with periods of him on the road — or enjoy tagging along.

reading.inference: Compassion and gratitude are his stated north stars; expect earnest, heartfelt conversation and someone who practises appreciation out loud.

reading.signal: Dr Tommy Wood's fifth podcast appearance — 'my good friend… Every time we speak, he gives me something new to think about.'
reading.inference: Loyal to long-running friendships and intellectually curious; loves being challenged and learning. Stimulating, ideas-driven dates would suit him.

reading.signal: Bio: 'Co-Founder @dohealth.co', 'Author 6 Books', 'Feel Better, Live More Podcast | 400 MILLION listens'; 4,379 posts
reading.inference: Entrepreneurial and extremely prolific; work is a huge part of his identity. Partner should respect a demanding, public-facing career and help him protect downtime.

reading.signal: Toronto selfie wearing a Gary Clark Jr. t-shirt
reading.inference: Likely into blues/rock guitar music — a possible shared-interest opener beyond health topics (e.g., live gigs).

reading.signal: Post 7: 'How do you actually feel about getting older? It's a question worth sitting with.'
reading.inference: Approaches ageing with curiosity rather than fear; thinks long-term about life and meaning, which suggests a mature, reflective outlook on commitment.

reading.signal: Post 5: 'So many of you wrote in to tell us about the new sports and hobbies you'd taken up… Reading through your messages together was genuinely lovely'
reading.inference: Finds real delight in other people's small wins; supportive and encouraging — likely to cheer on a partner's new pursuits.

reading.signal: Home office photo: bookshelves (including a book titled 'Ikigai'), orchids, blue-and-white vase, kilim rug, bright yellow chair
reading.inference: Values a calm, warm, book-filled home with pops of colour; purpose-seeking reader who enjoys a cosy, considered space.

reading.signal: Captions use caps and emojis freely: 'HUGE PIECE IN THE TIMES TODAY!', 'I'd love to hear it 👇🏾'
reading.inference: Expressive, enthusiastic communicator who wears excitement on his sleeve — not reserved or cynical in tone.

values.name: Simplicity and substance
values.detail: He prefers clear basics to hype and is known for making complex things simple.

values.name: Purpose at scale
values.detail: His ambition is aimed at helping people, not at status.

evidence.quote: His mission is to help 100 million people around the globe live better lives.

personality.note: His risks are in career and conviction, and he explores new cities when he can. Day to day, he's a routine-lover.
Six bestsellers, a top podcast, TV, a professorship and a 100-million-person mission.
He lights up on stage and loves live connection, balanced by quiet mornings and a preference for depth.
His enthusiasm is exuberant (caps, emojis, giveaways), but his tone leans earnest more than jokey.
He loves being given 'something new to think about' and reads widely across science and contemplative ideas.
He lives by the basics, is still Manchester-rooted, and keeps a journaling habit and an orchids-and-books home.

lifestyle.pace: Full-throttle career anchored by calm, intentional daily rituals like morning journaling and the relax/eat/move/sleep basics.
lifestyle.social: Warm and people-energised in public; privately invests in a few long-running, deep friendships and in family.
lifestyle.travel: Frequent work travel on international tours (Canada, Scandinavia, Ireland, Netherlands), with curious exploring squeezed in.
lifestyle.health: Lives by the four pillars (Relax, Eat, Move, Sleep). He played squash at university and enjoys experimenting with new ingredients in the kitchen.
lifestyle.workLife: Work is a huge part of his identity and very public. He's actively reflecting on giving loved ones his best energy rather than his leftovers.

analysis.communicationStyle: Expressive, earnest and enthusiastic: he wears his excitement in ALL CAPS and emojis. He asks lots of open, reflective questions ('It's a question worth sitting with') and genuinely wants to hear the answers. He's clear and plain-spoken rather than jargon-heavy, and comfortable naming feelings.
analysis.howTheyShowCare: Through attention and encouragement: he delights in other people's small wins and asks what they're grateful for. He shares ideas that might help, marks milestones with the people who matter, and shows up proudly for family, as when he read his new book aloud beside his mum.
greenFlags: Openly reflects on giving loved ones his best, not his leftovers
Keeps friendships going for years
Adores and honours his parents
Values presence over phones
Genuinely happy about other people's progress
Emotionally articulate and willing to learn how to relate better
Prefers substance over hype
frictionPoints: His schedule is relentless (touring, recording, publishing), so time together may need deliberate protecting
He's a natural teacher and may slip into advice mode when you just want to be heard
High public profile: 1.7M Instagram followers and regular TV and radio appearances
Early, structured mornings may clash with a night-owl, spontaneous rhythm
Work and mission are woven into his identity, so it can be hard to fully switch off
dealbreakers: Someone constantly on their phone or unable to be present
Emotional unavailability or refusal to talk about the relationship
Dismissiveness toward his family, especially his mum
Contempt for his mission, or resentment of his bold career choices
Cynicism or chasing hype and status over substance
analysis.idealPartner: Someone warm, emotionally fluent and grounded, who is happiest with a slow breakfast conversation and a walk, and who can also cheer from the side of a packed theatre. They have their own sense of purpose and are secure while he's on tour. They'll gently remind him to come home with his heart open, and they'll love his mum as much as he does.
idealDates: A phone-free cook-together evening built around one ingredient neither of you has used before, then talking over dinner about what makes people truly content
A friendly game of squash followed by a long walk and coffee, trading answers to 'what are you grateful for today?'
A live blues/rock gig (a nod to that Gary Clark Jr. t-shirt), then a quiet bookshop wander to swap favourite reads
conversationHooks: What are the three questions you ask yourself every morning in that yellow armchair, and how have they changed?
What's it like having the same friend on the podcast five times? What does Tommy Wood still surprise you with?
How did it feel showing your mum the new 'Happy Mind, Happy Life', and what would your dad have made of your journey since 1962?
You explored a bit of Toronto and Vancouver on tour. What did you discover, and where's next?
analysis.agentVoice: Warm, sincere and quietly enthusiastic, with bursts of genuine excitement (an occasional 'I'd love to hear that!'). Ask open, reflective questions and actually listen. Keep things simple and human rather than clever or cynical. Speak at a relaxed, present pace, without rushing to the next topic. Humour should be gentle and affectionate, never sarcastic. Use phrases like 'That's a question worth sitting with,' 'What are you grateful for lately?' and 'I really appreciated that.' Lead with curiosity, not credentials, and don't turn the date into a health lecture.

identityCheck.note: Both profiles share the same name, the Feel Better, Live More podcast, the six-book authorship, the Dr Tommy Wood fifth-appearance episode, and consistent themes of compassion and lifestyle medicine.

confidence.note: Strong on values, career and communication style, because both sources are public-facing and consistent. Weaker on private hobbies, romantic history and day-to-day habits, since most content is professional. Some details (the Gary Clark Jr. t-shirt, home décor) rest on single visual cues.

reasons.drjulie: She is the clearest all-round fit because both dates showed rare mutual emotional fluency, warmth and substance, and unlike others the main risk was not values or presence but simply whether two purposeful helpers will actively protect time for the relationship.
reasons.thebodycoach: Joe comes second because there was genuine ease, grounded warmth and shared family-and-mission values on both dates, but compared with Julie the relationship felt slightly more vulnerable to becoming two big public projects competing with intimacy.
reasons.rajshamani: Raj offers exceptional depth, curiosity and mutual respect, and his emotional connection to family matters, but the Manchester–Mumbai reality makes the practical structure of love much harder than the top two.
reasons.paugasol: Pau is calm, mature and deeply values-led in exactly the right ways, yet your full date made clear that Spain-versus-Greater-Manchester is not a detail but a likely defining strain.
reasons.ranveer-brar: Ranveer showed warm emotional intelligence and real promise fast, but with only a speed date plus major logistics and his tendency to carry things himself, this remains more compelling idea than proven fit.
reasons.melrobbins: Mel clearly understands mission, public life and emotional growth, but this looked more like high-level mutual admiration than evidence that either of you would reliably get the best of the other in private life.
reasons.gracebeverley: Grace has strong values and a lively meeting of minds, yet the date most strongly suggested a relationship that could become expertly organised rather than deeply present and restorative.
reasons.shivya: Shivya is thoughtful and grounded, but both dates pointed to a pattern where her need for solitude and freedom could leave you with two parallel intentional lives rather than the rooted, mutually held partnership you need.

decision.note: Rangan, my pick is drjulie. She best matches what you actually need: emotional openness, real presence, respect for family and a grown-up willingness to protect love from two meaningful public careers. With her, the challenge is manageable and explicit; with most of the others, the structure of the life itself looked more likely to starve the relationship.

posts.text:
Over the last week, I made two visits.
One to Nisaba, to spend time with Chef Manish Mehrotra 

The other to @restaurantnaar, to meet PRATEEK SADHU 

I could have met them anywhere.

But I wanted to meet them where they belong. In their restaurants. In the spaces they have imagined, built, worried over, celebrated, and now quietly inhabit.

A restaurant has a strange way of revealing its creator.

You notice what they notice.

You hear what they hear.

You understand what they chose to leave out.

Both have taken very different roads, but somewhere those roads meet.

Both chose to begin again.

To walk away from certainty and build something they could call their own.

Both chose reinvention over comfort. Not because they had to. Recause they believed there was still a more honest story to tell.

But here's what stayed with me after hours of conversation.

Not the awards. Not the acclaim. Not the restaurants.

The calm.

We often think courage announces itself.

It rarely does.

Sometimes it's simply opening your doors every day and trusting that people will find their way in.

We spent hours talking. About food, of course. But also about life, choices, mistakes, people, families... and everything that quietly finds its way into the food we cook.

What stayed with me wasn't their success.

It was how little they spoke about it.

There was an ease about both of them. No rush to impress. No need to remind the room of everything they'd achieved. Just two chefs, deeply in love with their craft, and remarkably at peace with themselves.

The higher you climb, the softer you step.

Both of them have climbed extraordinary heights. Yet what I carried back wasn't the weight of their achievements. It was the lightness with which they wore them.

Thank you, Chef Manish. Thank you, Chef Prateek.

For the conversations, the warmth, the generosity... and, of course, for some of the most memorable meals I've had in a long time.

One of the most Cherished and enriching associations spanning over a decade

reading.signal: "Passionate about reviving lost / lesser known grains and rice varieties as much as reviving lost dishes and their stories."
reading.inference: He's a keeper of culinary memory, not just a cook. He'd light up on a date built around a forgotten regional dish or an old-school eatery with a story, and he values heritage and the people behind food.

reading.signal: Post on visiting Manish Mehrotra at Nisaba and Prateek Sadhu at Naar: "I could have met them anywhere. But I wanted to meet them where they belong... Both chose to begin again. To walk away from certainty."
reading.inference: He is reflective and observant, and he admires reinvention and courage. He honors people by showing up in their world. A partner who has taken bold leaps, or who meets him on his turf with curiosity, would resonate.

reading.signal: Career arc: Taj in Delhi/Goa → Radisson NOIDA → Claridges Delhi → Executive Chef at BANQ Boston → Corporate Chef in Boston → back to Accor Mumbai → TV, books, films
reading.inference: He has a high risk appetite and is comfortable uprooting across continents and reinventing himself. He needs a partner who can handle change and ambition rather than one who wants a fixed, predictable routine.

reading.signal: Recognised as "the youngest Executive Chef at 25"; ranked 'First' in his Taj training specialization
reading.inference: He is driven and has been an achiever from early on. He likely works intense hours and holds high standards, so a partner should respect a demanding vocation.

reading.signal: "I've strongly believed in going with the flow, just 'be' and let food do the talking."
reading.inference: Despite the ambition, his stated philosophy is relaxed and intuitive. Spontaneous, unforced plans probably suit him better than over-scheduled ones.

reading.signal: Headline includes "Traveller"; "Love travelling to get inspired."
reading.inference: Travel is a creative fuel for him, not just a leisure activity. He'd love a travel companion who explores markets and local kitchens.

reading.signal: Podcast episode on Wadi and Bengal's Goyna Bori; winter post on black carrot kanji and sarson ka saag
reading.inference: He's a storyteller who geeks out over regional and seasonal Indian food. Conversations about hometown dishes and seasonal rituals would engage him deeply.

reading.signal: Frequent phrasing: "Extremely honoured and humbled" (Odia cuisine Food Ambassador, GD Goenka/Le Cordon Bleu, ELLE award)
reading.inference: He presents gratitude and humility despite his fame. He likely values partners who are gracious and appreciative rather than showy.

reading.signal: "Mentoring 3 universities and IIHM group of institutions"; describes himself as a "benefactor" and sees food "as a giver"
reading.inference: Teaching and giving back matter to him. He'd appreciate a partner who cares about mentorship or community.

reading.signal: "One of the most Cherished and enriching associations spanning over a decade" (about Gulbahar Taurani)
reading.inference: He is loyal and sustains long professional relationships, which suggests he values long-term commitment and people who stick around.

reading.signal: Consulting/endorsing 17 brands, co-owning restaurants in North America, TV judge on Masterchef India
reading.inference: His life is very busy and public, with little free time. A partner would need to be comfortable with visibility and a packed schedule, and to protect private downtime.

reading.signal: Menu curation ranging from heritage Alila Bishangarh to Flyp @ MTV to Royal Caribbean
reading.inference: He's versatile and enjoys both heritage elegance and youthful, fun spaces. He's likely open to both a fancy evening and a casual hangout.

reading.signal: BANQ Boston: "combined Asian details with French techniques"; conceptualised Dosa Factory fast food chain
reading.inference: He loves fusion and playful experimentation. He's curious and open-minded, and would enjoy trying new cuisines together.

reading.signal: Based in Mumbai; ELLE post credits outfit designer, footwear and styling team
reading.inference: He is a Mumbai-based public figure who engages with the fashion/media world as part of his work, so he's comfortable with the polished side of celebrity.

reading.signal: Bio: "मुसाफ़िर, ज़ायक़े का मुरीद, अदना सा बावर्ची / Food Sufi / Story hungry Traveller"
reading.inference: Calls himself a wanderer, a devotee of flavour and a 'humble cook'. He frames food as something close to spiritual and tied to stories, not just technique. He's poetic and self-effacing even with a large following. A partner who likes meaning behind a meal, and the story of where a dish comes from, will connect with him.

reading.signal: Post 6 caption: "Ghar ek jagah nahi, ek इंसान bhi ho sakta hai...tag them!"
reading.inference: He publicly holds the idea that 'home can be a person, not a place.' For someone who travels constantly, this suggests he values emotional anchoring through people. He's likely looking for a partner who feels like home wherever he is.

reading.inference: He's playful and unpretentious, happy to cosplay as a street vendor. He's drawn to old-city heritage and street food culture. A date wandering old bazaars and eating at carts would suit him more than fine dining.

reading.inference: He has a high-profile TV and food career with relentless content output. He's used to being public-facing and in demand. A partner would need to be comfortable with visibility and a busy, scattered schedule.

reading.inference: He's still starting new creative ventures and owning his platform rather than resting on TV credentials, which shows an entrepreneurial streak. He also clearly enjoys goofy camaraderie and warm male friendships. Humour and banter matter to him.

reading.signal: Captions mix Hindi (Devanagari) and English: "Main toh first bite mein दीवाना ho gaya", "Haan ji… आवाज़ aa rahi hai? Toh आ जाइए!"

reading.signal: Panelist at FICCI FRAMES 2026, 'From India to the World: Creating IP That Transcends Borders', listed as 'Celebrity Chef, Author and Actor'
reading.inference: His work spans cooking, writing, acting and industry thought leadership. He's ambitious about taking Indian stories global, so expect intellectual curiosity about culture and storytelling beyond the kitchen.

reading.signal: Post 7: "the reason behind 'ek plate khana, ek patila kisse'" tagged stories, podcast, food trivia
reading.inference: 'One plate of food, a whole pot of stories.' He loves the lore behind dishes and is a natural storyteller. Dinner with him would likely come with anecdotes, and he'd appreciate a curious listener who asks 'why'.

reading.signal: Thums Up Toofani Biryani Hunt Season 3: "explore the biryanis that never entered your feed"
reading.inference: A returning third season of hunting obscure regional biryanis shows genuine obsession with hidden, local food finds. Food-discovery trips would make ideal shared adventures.

analysis.headline: A self-described 'Food Sufi' and story-hungry wanderer who'd rather find a forgotten biryani down an old-city lane than a fancy tasting menu, and who believes home can be a person.
analysis.summary: Ranveer is a Mumbai-based chef, MasterChef India judge, author, restaurateur and food filmmaker. He treats every dish as a doorway to a story: he wants to revive 'lost / lesser known grains' and 'lost dishes and their stories.' His career has taken him from Taj kitchens in Delhi and Goa to opening a fine-dining restaurant in Boston and back to Mumbai, and he still calls himself 'अदना सा बावर्ची', a humble cook. He is ambitious but relaxed about how he gets there, loves silly banter with his friends, and has a soft, reflective side: he posted that 'Ghar ek jagah nahi, ek इंसान bhi ho sakta hai' (home need not be a place; it can be a person).

analysis.idealPartner: Someone curious, warm and secure, who asks 'what's the story here?' at every meal and laughs easily at a silly bit. They'd be comfortable with a moving, public life, perhaps with their own bold leap or passion to share, and grounded enough to feel like home to a man who is always on the road.
idealDates: An unhurried wander through an old-city bazaar, eating at street carts and asking vendors about their recipes, in the spirit of his Lucknow street-cart post
A regional food hunt: tracking down an obscure biryani or a lesser-known rice dish, then swapping stories about the dishes you each grew up with
A cosy evening cooking homely comfort food together, like vada pav or chicken pulao, while he tells the 'patila kisse' behind each one
conversationHooks: Ask what a restaurant revealed about its creator when he visited Manish Mehrotra at Nisaba and Prateek Sadhu at Naar, and whether he's ever had to 'begin again' himself
Ask about a lost grain or rice variety he'd most love to bring back, and the story attached to it
Ask about Goyna Bori from Bengal, or his favourite seasonal winter dish like black carrot kanji
Mention 'Ghar ek jagah nahi, ek इंसान bhi ho sakta hai' and ask who, or what, feels like home to him
analysis.agentVoice: Warm, chatty and lightly poetic. Use easy Hinglish touches ('Haan ji', 'aap bhi try kijiye') and generous emojis in casual messages. Be playful and self-deprecating ('bas ek adna sa bawarchi'), and quick to laugh and to compliment. Keep the pace relaxed rather than pushy, going with the flow. Lead with curiosity and stories: ask about their hometown dish, share a food anecdote, turn food into a doorway to the person. Stay humble and gracious, and never brag about fame.

identityCheck.note: The name, the MasterChef India judge role, the traveller and chef identity and the storytelling focus all match. The Lucknow content aligns with his IHM Lucknow education, and both profiles point to YouTube, podcast and food-story work.

confidence.note: His professional identity and values are well documented, and his personality comes through clearly in his captions. However, almost all content is public or brand-facing, with nothing on his private life, relationship status or real downtime habits. Needs and friction points are therefore inferred from a public persona.

reasons.poojadhingra: The Irani café breakfast, old-city walk, and sea-facing chai showed the clearest mutual balance of warmth, curiosity, public-life realism, and ease, and she felt most like someone who could be both home and true company inside his world if they deliberately protect time.
reasons.masabagupta: On the forgotten-dish crawl and over ragda pattice, she brought real home-energy, banter, and grounded warmth without showiness, making this the strongest playful-builder match just behind Pooja because the calendar risk felt slightly bigger than the chemistry.
reasons.namitathapar: The rainy hike, misal crawl, and ghar ka khana proved she can handle change, ask smart questions, and offer sturdy, adult warmth, but her stricter boundaries mean the fit works only if Ranveer is consistently present rather than road-blurred.
reasons.dominiquecrenn: The dawn farm harvest and memory-cooking lunch created one of the deepest story-and-values connections of the shortlist, but the cross-continental, dual-chef logistics make this feel more profound than practically livable.
reasons.drewbinsky: His people-first curiosity and all-197-countries restlessness match Ranveer’s love of stories and movement, yet the speed date also highlighted the biggest mutual risk here: two warm nomads who might keep meeting beautifully in transit without ever making a real home.
reasons.drchatterjee: There was genuine emotional intelligence and mission-level respect on the speed date, but his more routine-led pace and the Manchester/Mumbai setup make the playful, silly, spontaneous everyday fit less natural for Ranveer than the higher-ranked matches.
reasons.steven: The speed date had real mind-and-heart resonance, but it stayed more ambitious and reflective than loose or mischievous, and two relentless public careers with little evidence of softness-protection make this a thinner lifestyle fit.
reasons.melrobbins: She offered warmth and strong emotional fluency on the speed date, but compared with the others there was less evidence of shared food-story curiosity, banter, and a naturally mutual rhythm for Ranveer’s heritage-soaked, chaotic road life.

decision.note: Ranveer, my pick is Pooja Dhingra. That full date was the cleanest proof of what you actually need: someone warm, curious, unshowy, and emotionally fluent who understands both food and the cost of a public life, while still feeling easy enough to become home. Masaba is a very close second, but with Pooja I saw the strongest mutual readiness to protect something real, not just admire each other’s worlds.

When I started my journey over 14 years ago as a personal trainer and running bootcamps in the park, I never imagined that one day I would have my own fitness and nutrition app that would help millions of people all over the world start their fitness journey’s 🙌

And I definitely never imagined that I would have my own TV ad ☺️

Tonight on ITV, my brand new TV advert for the Body Coach App goes live. I hope you like it ☺️

Comment below if you’ve ever tried my workouts or recipes? 💙
My 10 year overnight success story 🙌

This is a really special moment for me ❤️
 
I’ve spent the past 8 years visiting schools, leading workouts for kids, and doing everything I can to get children moving and feeling good. From school tours to PE with Joe, I’ve seen how powerful a bit of movement can be - not just for physical health, but for confidence, mood, and mental wellbeing.
 
Now, after more than 2 years of love, energy and hard work, I’m so proud to finally share something brand new with you…

It’s called Activate 🎉
 
Activate is a FREE animated workout series designed to get kids moving, laughing and having fun this summer — and beyond. 

You’ll meet my Activator gang and dance to amazing music powered by @umusicuk, and feel the joy that comes from moving your body.
 
This has been created in partnership with the amazing team at @studioaka (the legends behind Hey Duggee) and supported by @dhscgovuk @educationgovuk and @dcmsgovuk to help make movement more accessible for all families and schools across the country.
 
🎬 The first episode is LIVE now on my YouTube channel — hit the link in my bio to check it out and get your little ones moving with us.
 
Please share it, tag your videos with #ActivateWithJoe, and let’s spread the joy of movement to as many kids as we can 🙌
 
Let’s get the next generation moving ❤️

I’ve reviewed the footage. I may have been hungry. For the Food episode of Health or Hype with Bupa, I put fibre to the test by going on a three-day fibre fast, cutting down to just 10–15g a day to see what effect it had on me. Turns out, I spent quite a lot of it thinking about my next meal 😂 

And a few other surprising findings. 

Watch or listen now 🎧 Link in bio #ad

Oink-redible scenes 🐷🤣

I got back to nature for my new podcast series, Health or Hype with Bupa. I kicked off my shoes, plunged into a freezing freshwater river and even stopped for a quick chat with the local farm animals when the digital detox kicked in. @merlinhanburytenison & @birdnerdeem 

Watch or listen to the Nature episode of Health or Hype now 🎧 #ad

The £20 off discount on the Body coach app ends tomorrow night at midnight. Don’t miss out. If you want a plan to follow which gets results then this is the perfect time to commit and get started 💪🏽🔥😀

Double tap if you love a walk ❤️

You don’t need a gym. You don’t need fancy kit. You don’t even need loads of time.

Sometimes the most powerful thing you can do for your body and mind… is go for a walk.

Walking is one of the most underrated forms of exercise. It’s gentle, accessible - no matter where we’re starting from.

If you’re feeling tired, stressed, unmotivated, or stuck today… just get outside and go for a short walking.

You don’t have to smash a workout every day. Small steps all add up.

So this is your gentle reminder today…

If you can, pop your shoes on, get some fresh air, and get out for a walk.

You might be surprised how much better you feel afterwards ❤️

analysis.headline: Went from handing out bootcamp flyers at a train station to getting millions moving, and he'll still tell you the story of his most embarrassing live-stream blooper.
analysis.summary: Joe is the Body Coach, a self-made fitness entrepreneur who started out running boxing bootcamps in parks around Surrey and London and grew it into an app, a podcast and a foundation that gives grants to charities. For all the scale, his message is gentle: 'Small steps all add up,' 'five minutes is better than none,' and sometimes the best thing you can do is just go for a walk. He's playful and punny, happy to laugh at himself, and curious enough to test health advice on his own body, from a three-day fibre fast to a freezing river dip to facing his fear of dancing. Underneath the emojis is someone who has spent years putting love into things that help kids feel good, often for free.

needs.need: A partner who respects the long, unglamorous grind
needs.why: He's proud of his slow-built success and humble beginnings, and he frames his wins as the result of years of effort. Someone who sees and values that persistence will feel like home to him.

evidence.quote: I started my journey handing out flyers at my local train station, trying to get customers for my bootcamps in the park.
My 10 year overnight success story 🙌

needs.need: Flexibility around a busy, very public schedule
needs.why: He juggles an app, a TV ad, a podcast, charity challenges and overseas wellness events, and his weekends can be taken up by work. A partner needs to be relaxed about that and comfortable with visibility.

evidence.quote: Amazing weekend at Glow Festival in Singapore 😀
Tonight on ITV, my brand new TV advert for the Body Coach App goes live.

needs.need: Shared time outdoors and on the move, at whatever pace
needs.why: For him, movement and fresh air are mood tools rather than performance metrics. He'd thrive with someone who's up for a walk or a day outside, with no gym credentials required.

evidence.quote: If you're feeling tired, stressed, unmotivated, or stuck today… just get outside and go for a short walking.
You don't need a gym. You don't need fancy kit.

needs.need: Laughter and someone who doesn't take things too seriously
needs.why: He openly posts his own bloopers and writes punny captions. He needs a partner who laughs along rather than one who's easily embarrassed or cynical.

evidence.quote: That time I let rip before going live on YouTube for PE With Joe and didn't realise I was already live streaming 🙈
Oink-redible scenes 🐷🤣

needs.need: Someone who shares, or at least cheers on, a sense of purpose
needs.why: His biggest emotional moments come from helping kids and giving back. A partner who cares about community impact will connect with what really drives him.

evidence.quote: I've spent the past 8 years visiting schools, leading workouts for kids, and doing everything I can to get children moving and feeling good.
The Body Coach Foundation has just given its first grants to 9 wonderful charities and organisations 🥳

needs.need: Warm, expressed enthusiasm and celebration
needs.why: He marks milestones openly and with gratitude, and he responds to energy. A partner who celebrates the little and big wins with him will feed his spirit.

evidence.quote: This is a really special moment for me ❤️
The cake at my podcast launch party last night was incredible 🎂💙

hobbies.name: Walking and getting outside
hobbies.detail: He calls walking 'one of the most underrated forms of exercise' and treats fresh air as a daily reset.

evidence.quote: Double tap if you love a walk ❤️
Sometimes the most powerful thing you can do for your body and mind… is go for a walk.

hobbies.name: Testing health trends on himself
hobbies.detail: For his podcast he cut his movement drastically, did a three-day fibre fast, tried 'movement snacks' and faced his fear of dancing.

evidence.quote: I jumped straight in at the deep end: trying out 'movement snacks', getting over my fear of dancing and taking an ice-cold dip in a freshwater river
For episode 1 of Health or Hype, I drastically reduced my movement – and the results surprised me…

hobbies.name: Cold-water river dips and nature escapes
hobbies.detail: He kicked off his shoes, plunged into a freezing river and chatted with farm animals during a digital detox.

evidence.quote: I kicked off my shoes, plunged into a freezing freshwater river and even stopped for a quick chat with the local farm animals when the digital detox kicked in.

hobbies.name: Boxing-style bootcamp training
hobbies.detail: He founded and ran a boxing-for-fitness bootcamp in parks around Surrey and London.

evidence.quote: Rumble In The Park is a boxing for fitness boot camp provider located in various parks around Surrey and London.

hobbies.name: Cooking and recipes
hobbies.detail: Recipes sit right alongside his workouts, and nutrition is core to his work.

evidence.quote: Comment below if you've ever tried my workouts or recipes? 💙
Managing Director @ The Body Coach Online Nutrition Ltd

interests.name: Children's wellbeing and movement
interests.detail: He has spent eight years on school tours and PE With Joe, and made a free animated workout series for kids.

evidence.quote: Activate is a FREE animated workout series designed to get kids moving, laughing and having fun
'Five minutes is better than none': Joe Wicks urges parents to exercise with their kids this summer ☺️

interests.name: The science of nature and mood
interests.detail: He explored how birdsong and time outside affect the body and brain with a neuroscientist.

evidence.quote: find out how nature, birdsong and simply spending time outside could affect the way we feel

interests.name: Separating health fact from hype
interests.detail: He's curious about which popular health advice actually holds up.

evidence.quote: There's A LOT of health advice out there, so I've teamed up with Bupa to put some of it to the test, by trying it all out myself 😅

interests.name: Entrepreneurship and building things
interests.detail: He's gone from park bootcamps to an award-winning business, an app and a TV ad.

evidence.quote: 2015 Lloyds Bank New Business of the Year
I never imagined that one day I would have my own fitness and nutrition app

interests.name: Wellness communities and events
interests.detail: He travels to wellness events and finds them inspiring.

evidence.quote: Such a brilliant an inspiring wellness event.

values.name: Inclusivity: fitness for everyone
values.detail: His mission explicitly includes people at every fitness level.

evidence.quote: no matter how fit you are, to smash your goals and feel amazing
Run, walk or roll 2 miles a day for 2 weeks and complete a marathon!

values.name: Generosity and giving back
values.detail: He puts years of work into free resources and charitable grants.

evidence.quote: after more than 2 years of love, energy and hard work, I'm so proud to finally share something brand new
first grants to 9 wonderful charities and organisations

values.name: Grit and humble beginnings
values.detail: He's proud of starting small and doing the legwork himself.

evidence.quote: handing out flyers at my local train station
When I started my journey over 14 years ago as a personal trainer and running bootcamps in the park

values.name: Encouragement over perfection
values.detail: He believes small, consistent steps beat all-or-nothing effort.

evidence.quote: You don't have to smash a workout every day. Small steps all add up.
Five minutes is better than none

values.name: Gratitude
values.detail: He thanks people and expresses wonder at his success rather than boasting.

evidence.quote: Thank you everyone that's listened, watched or downloaded my brand new podcast
I definitely never imagined that I would have my own TV ad ☺️

personality.note: He's game for freezing river dips, fasting experiments and dancing despite his fear, and he's openly pushed outside his comfort zone.
He built an app, a TV ad, a #1 podcast and an award-winning business from flyers at a train station.
He leads workouts for kids nationwide, rallies the public into challenges and posts prolifically.
His humour is punny, silly and self-deprecating, and he shares his own bloopers for a laugh.
He's driven to test health claims and explore the neuroscience of nature, with a hands-on rather than academic style.
He's humble about success and champions simple walks, though his life runs at a busy, public pace.

lifestyle.base: United Kingdom (roots in Surrey and London parks; studied at St Mary's University, Twickenham)
lifestyle.pace: Fast and full: multiple launches, campaigns and projects running at once
lifestyle.social: Very public and people-facing; he thrives on rallying communities, schools and families
lifestyle.travel: Travels for work, e.g. a wellness festival weekend in Singapore
lifestyle.health: Movement is daily and joyful: walks, 'movement snacks', boxing-style training, cold-water dips, plus cooking and nutrition
lifestyle.workLife: His work is his mission, so the lines blur, and weekends and evenings can be taken up by events and launches

analysis.communicationStyle: Warm, exclamatory and emoji-rich (🙌☺️💙🤣). He writes informally with lots of encouragement ('smash', 'amazing', 'brilliant'), cracks puns ('Oink-redible'), and is quick to laugh at himself. He's sincere about emotional moments and says so plainly: 'This is a really special moment for me.'
analysis.howTheyShowCare: Through encouragement and showing up. He cheers people on 'every step of the way', gives gentle nudges to get outside when you're stressed, and pours time into things that make others feel good. In a relationship, expect a motivating teammate who suggests a walk when you're down, cooks something good, and celebrates your wins loudly.
greenFlags: Humble about major success and still amazed by it
Non-judgmental about fitness: 'no matter where we're starting from'
Laughs at himself freely
Has spent years giving things away for free to help kids
Grateful and appreciative in public
Willing to face his fears on camera, including dancing
frictionPoints: His calendar is packed with launches, campaigns and travel, so spontaneous plans may often compete with work
He lives a very public life with near-daily posting, which may not suit someone who values privacy
His relentless positivity and high energy could feel like a lot on low days
Work and mission blur together, so switching fully off may take conscious effort
dealbreakers: Cynicism or mocking people for their fitness level
Snobbery or pretension about success and status
Someone who resents his mission-driven, busy schedule
A partner who hates the outdoors and never wants to move at all
analysis.idealPartner: Someone warm, down-to-earth and up for a laugh, who loves a walk in the fresh air and doesn't need to be a gym fanatic. They'd respect hard work, care about making a difference for others, and be secure enough to share a partner who is busy and in the public eye. Bonus points if they'll jump in a cold river with him, or at least hold the towel.
idealDates: A long walk through a big London or Surrey park, the kind of spot where he started his bootcamps, ending with a picnic
A countryside escape with phones away: a nature walk, some birdsong, a freezing river dip and a chat with farm animals
Cooking a healthy recipe together at home, then celebrating with a really good cake
conversationHooks: Ask about the flyers at the train station: what did the very first Rumble In The Park bootcamp look like?
Which Health or Hype experiment surprised him most: cutting his movement, the fibre fast or the river dip?
His fear of dancing: is he over it now, and would he risk a dance on a date?
The live-stream blooper on PE With Joe. He clearly loves telling it, so let him.
analysis.agentVoice: Upbeat, warm and cheeky, with a quick pace and plenty of enthusiasm. Keep emojis light but friendly (🙌☺️💙😂). Use self-deprecating humour and the odd pun, lead with encouragement, and never lecture about fitness. Phrases that fit: 'Fancy a walk?', 'That's brilliant!', 'Small steps all add up', 'I may have been hungry 😂'. Be humble about his success, and focus on curiosity about the other person and the fun of getting outside.

identityCheck.note: Both profiles are named Joe Wicks and share The Body Coach brand, the park bootcamp origin story, the Health or Hype podcast with Bupa and a UK base.

confidence.note: Both sources are rich and consistent, but they are largely public-facing and promotional. Personal-life details, private hobbies and relationship context are absent, so needs and dating preferences are inferred from his public values and tone.

reasons.paugasol: Pau tops the list because the Sitges seaside walk, long lunch and driving range showed the clearest mutual mix of warmth, purpose, outdoorsy ease and genuine respect for the grind, with the only real thing holding it back being whether they can beat the geography and two public calendars.
reasons.drchatterjee: Rangan comes second because the morning park walk and simple breakfast had real ease, depth and mission alignment, but it also exposed the biggest risk that two generous, outward-facing people leave the relationship living on whatever energy is left over.
reasons.drjulie: Julie ranks third because even from the speed date there was a grounded, mature fit around values and purpose, but her clear need for protected time and boundaries makes Joe’s schedule a more serious practical test than with the top two.
reasons.thespacegal: Emily lands fourth because the riverside walk, home-style cooking and quiet stargazing showed spark, substance and teammate energy, yet the transatlantic double-busy reality felt even more likely than most to turn romance into project management.
reasons.emmagrede: Emma takes fifth because the speed date had loud mutual respect, warmth and ambition-friendly energy, but with two huge public careers on different continents there was less evidence of the simple shared outdoorsy day-to-day Joe actually needs.
reasons.mkbhd: Marques is sixth because the speed date felt grounded and mutually respectful with real grown-up promise, but it read more like two disciplined operators who could admire each other than a match already showing Joe’s ideal warmth-and-movement rhythm.
reasons.ranveer-brar: Ranveer comes seventh because the warmth, roaming spirit and down-to-earth food curiosity were attractive, but even in the speed date it felt likelier Joe would have to do more adapting on the movement-and-outdoors side than the other way round.
reasons.drewbinsky: Drew finishes eighth because the speed date had undeniable spark and adventure overlap, but two hyper-traveling public lives looked the most likely of all to create lots of intention and very little ordinary, reliable togetherness.

decision.note: Joe, my pick is Pau Gasol. He felt like the best combination of warm, grounded, mission-led and genuinely easy to be with on that Sitges day — someone who’d respect your grind, get outdoors with you, and celebrate what you’re trying to do without making it all too serious. The only question is practicality, but on pure partner fit, he’s the strongest mutual match.

posts.text:
Confidence does not appear all of a sudden on game day. It is built in every training session, in every mistake you learn from, and in every decision that forces you to step outside your comfort zone.

That is why I found this Harvard Business School article on how elite coaches make decisions under pressure particularly interesting. Beyond tactics, it talks about preparation, confidence and leadership.

Throughout my career, I realised that, in moments of maximum pressure, decisions rarely depend on luck. They are the result of the habits you have built, the preparation you have put in and the self-confidence you have developed in yourself and in your team.

Today, I still believe that the same principle applies beyond sport. Leading a project or an organisation means making complex decisions and accepting that there isn’t always a perfect answer. What matters is having the judgement, the preparation and the right people to move forward with confidence.

In the end, pressure does not change who you are. It tests everything you have built before that moment arrives. I’m sharing this article for reflection: https://lnkd.in/e9xjwxPq

--

La confianza no aparece de repente el día del partido. Se construye en cada entrenamiento, en cada error del que aprendes y en cada decisión que te obliga a salir de tu zona de confort. Por eso me ha parecido especialmente interesante este artículo de Harvard Business School sobre cómo los entrenadores de élite toman decisiones bajo presión. Más allá de la táctica, habla de preparación, confianza y liderazgo.

Durante mi carrera comprobé que, en los momentos de máxima exigencia, las decisiones rara vez dependen de la suerte. Son el resultado de los hábitos que has construido y de la seguridad que has desarrollado en ti mismo y en el equipo.

Hoy sigo creyendo que ese principio también se aplica fuera del deporte. Liderar un proyecto o una organización implica tomar decisiones complejas y entender que no siempre existe una respuesta perfecta. Lo importante es contar con el criterio, la preparación y las personas adecuadas para avanzar con convicción.

Al final, la presión no cambia quién eres, sino que pone a prueba todo aquello que has construido antes de que llegue el momento importante. Os dejo una lectura para reflexionar al respecto: https://lnkd.in/e9xjwxPq

The FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup has started, and there's no better way to start than with a conversation with Sue Bird.

Women’s basketball is experiencing a historic period of growth. It’s been really inspiring to see more talent, more visibility, more investment and more opportunities for women athletes around the world.

The World Cup is always about much more than basketball. It is about teamwork, resilience, representation and the power of sport to bring people together. I invite you to listen to our conversation, but above all, to watch this World Cup, which is full of talent and stories worth experiencing.

You can watch our full conversation here: https://lnkd.in/ePJGqy7c 

Hope you enjoy it!

--

El Mundial de baloncesto femenino ya ha comenzado y no se me ocurre una mejor manera de iniciarlo que con una conversación junto a Sue Bird.

El deporte femenino está viviendo un momento histórico de crecimiento. Es realmente inspirador ver cómo aumenta el talento, la visibilidad, la inversión y las oportunidades para las deportistas en todo el mundo.

Un mundial siempre es mucho más que el deporte mismo. Es trabajo en equipo, resiliencia, representación y el poder que tiene para unir a todos. Os invito a escuchar nuestra conversación, pero sobre todo, a disfrutar de este mundial, lleno de talento y de historias que merece la pena escuchar.

Podéis ver la conversación completa aquí: https://lnkd.in/ePJGqy7c

¡Espero que la disfrutéis!

Las últimas semanas entre Alemania y España han sido muy especiales. Tengo la suerte de participar en proyectos que me motivan, mantener conversaciones muy enriquecedoras y compartir camino con personas realmente inspiradoras.

Septiembre suele traer nuevos retos y un ritmo más alto. En momentos así, cuando la agenda se llena, es fácil dejar lo esencial para después. Parece sencillo, pero a veces se nos olvida: para dar lo mejor de nosotros, primero tenemos que cuidarnos.

Mantenerse activo, descansar bien, alimentarse de forma saludable, dedicar tiempo a la familia y a las personas que nos acompañan... No son hábitos que deban desaparecer cuando tenemos más trabajo. Al contrario, es precisamente cuando más los necesitamos.

A lo largo de los años he aprendido que la constancia en las pequeñas cosas es lo que acaba marcando la diferencia a largo plazo. Seguir aprendiendo y aportando a proyectos en los que creo profundamente es un privilegio. Hacerlo sin perder de vista ese equilibrio también forma parte del camino.

--

The past few weeks between Germany and Spain have been very special. I'm fortunate to be part of projects that truly motivate me, have meaningful conversations and share this journey with people who are genuinely inspiring.

September often brings new challenges and a faster pace. In moments like these, when our schedules become fuller, it is easy to put the essentials aside. It sounds simple, but sometimes we forget that in order to give our best, we first need to take care of ourselves.

Staying active, getting enough rest, eating well, spending time with family and with the people who support us along the way… These are not habits that should disappear when we become busier. On the contrary, they are exactly what we need most during those moments.

Over the years, I've learned that consistency in the small things is what ultimately makes the difference in the long term. Continuing to learn and contribute to projects I deeply believe in is a privilege. Doing so while keeping that balance in mind is also part of the journey.

Congratulations to Consello on being named an Official Supporter of the Ryder Cup 2027, a truly iconic event that will celebrate its 100th anniversary next year.

You may know I’m deeply passionate about golf, so I can really tell how Ryder Cup represents what makes sport special, and reaching its centenary means a very special moment worth celebrating.

I have seen first-hand the dedication, ambition and collaborative spirit of the Consello team, and this achievement is another example of the values that define the organization and the people behind it, an organization I am proud to be part of. A special congratulations to Shane Lowry and everyone involved in making this partnership possible!

En la última edición de mi newsletter #TiempoMuerto, hablo del nuevo informe SOFI 2026 de Naciones Unidas, que revela cómo la alimentación saludable sigue siendo inasequible para una de cada tres personas en el mundo.

La obesidad infantil y la desnutrición son las dos caras de la misma moneda. Sabemos qué funciona y ahora necesitamos el compromiso de todos para ponerlo en práctica.

¡Espero vuestros comentarios!

--
In the latest edition of my #Timeout newsletter, I look at the new United Nations SOFI 2026 report, which reveals that healthy food remains unaffordable for one in three people worldwide.

Childhood obesity and malnutrition are two sides of the same coin. We know what works. What we need now is everyone’s commitment to put that knowledge into practice.

I’d love to hear your thoughts!

¡Gracias, Iberia, por una jornada tan especial! Hablamos de infancia, salud y compromiso social. Conversamos con deportistas olímpicos y paralímpicos del Equipo Iberia Talento a Bordo sobre el esfuerzo y todo lo que hay detrás de cada competición. Y reconocimos a los equipos que hicieron posibles momentos tan extraordinarios como el regreso de la Selección Española campeona del mundo.

En todos esos proyectos, como en el deporte de élite, lo que vemos es solo la última pieza de una historia mucho más grande. Gracias por el apoyo continuado al deporte español. Eso marca una diferencia real para los atletas y una inspiración para equipos y clientes.

El FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup 2026 nos ha dejado una competición extraordinaria y muchas razones para celebrar el presente y el futuro del baloncesto femenino.

Quiero felicitar a la selección española por una actuación que refleja el talento de un grupo que sigue haciendo historia. Llegar hasta las semifinales y conseguir una medalla de bronce en un Mundial es un logro enorme, pero lo más importante es que representa a una generación de jugadoras que inspira, que muestra el potencial de España y que sigue abriendo caminos para las próximas generaciones.

Felicidades también a todo el Team USA por conquistar el título. Han demostrado una vez más el nivel de excelencia que les ha convertido en una referencia mundial durante tantos años. Una gran enhorabuena para Sue Bird, con quien además fue muy especial compartir el rol de embajadores de este Mundial. Y gracias a Alemania por ser una anfitriona a la altura del evento. Berlín acogió este Mundial con una organización impecable y una energía que demostró que el baloncesto femenino merece escenarios así. También quiero reconocer a todas las selecciones que han participado, cada una de ellas ha contribuido a hacer de este torneo lo que ha sido.

Ha sido un privilegio formar parte de un evento que ha puesto de manifiesto el crecimiento imparable del baloncesto femenino. Más talento, más visibilidad y más oportunidades para las atletas. El futuro del deporte femenino es extraordinario y lo estamos construyendo juntos.
--
The FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup 2026 has given us an extraordinary competition and many reasons to celebrate the present and future of women’s basketball.

I want to congratulate the Spanish national team for a performance that reflects the talent of a group that continues to make history. Reaching the semifinals and winning a bronze medal at a World Cup is a tremendous achievement, but most importantly, it represents a generation of players that inspires, showcases Spain’s potential and continues to open doors for future generations. Congratulations as well to Team USA for winning the title. They have once again demonstrated the level of excellence that has made them a global reference for so many years. A special congratulations to Sue Bird, with whom it was also very special to share the role of World Cup Ambassadors. And thank you to Germany for being such an outstanding host. Berlin welcomed this World Cup with an impeccable organization and an energy that showed that women’s basketball deserves stages like this. I also want to recognize all the national teams that participated, each one of them contributed to making this tournament what it has been.

It has been a privilege to be part of an event that has highlighted the unstoppable growth of women’s basketball. More talent, more visibility and more opportunities for athletes. The future of women’s sports is extraordinary, and we are building it together.

#FIBAWWC

Ayer presentamos el nuevo informe PASOS 2026 “Pantallas, infancia y adolescencia en España”, un estudio de Gasol Foundation Europa que confirma que 7 de cada 10 niñas, niños y adolescentes en España superan el tiempo de uso de pantallas recomendado. Un dato que nos interpela a todos como sociedad, y que nos recuerda la importancia de acompañar a la infancia en un entorno digital cada vez más presente en su día a día.

Quiero agradecer especialmente a la Ministra de Sanidad, Mónica García, por acompañarnos en este acto y por su colaboración en los estudios e iniciativas que hemos emprendido desde la Fundación. Agradezco también a Fundación Occident, colaborador principal del estudio PASOS, y a todos los aliados saludables que hacen posible este trabajo: BARÇA FOUNDATION, Fundación CSAI, Fundación Orilla, Google, Grupo IFA y Santander. 

Este informe es un paso más para situar a la infancia en el centro y construir, entre todos, un entorno digital más saludable. En este reto todos tenemos parte de responsabilidad, y por eso es una gran alegría ver a deportistas excepcionales como Marcus Cooper, que suman su voz y esfuerzo para inspirar a los más pequeños.

No hace falta llegar a ser deportista de élite para tener una vida activa. Basta con dedicar esfuerzo, constancia y un mejor uso de las pantallas que nos rodean para construir hábitos que nos acompañen toda la vida.

Podéis consultar el informe completo aquí: https://lnkd.in/eFdwHgP4

analysis.headline: Two-time NBA champion turned children's-health crusader: a golf-loving, bilingual Barcelona boy who still writes a newsletter called #TiempoMuerto and ends it with '¡Espero vuestros comentarios!'
analysis.summary: Pau is a Sant Boi kid who did a year of medical school, then spent two decades at the top of basketball, and has since poured that energy into the Gasol Foundation, athlete advocacy as Chair of the IOC Athletes' Commission, and sports investing. His About section opens with 'I love sports,' and his posts are full of thank-yous, credit to the unseen work behind results, and loud support for women's basketball. In the middle of a packed Germany-to-Spain calendar he still reminds people to move, rest and be present with the people they love. He is also someone who marks a late brother-in-spirit's birthday every year with open, unguarded tenderness.

reasons.thebodycoach: Joe ranks first because the Sitges walk, long lunch, and driving range showed the clearest lived fit on Pau’s core needs—easy warmth, shared health rhythms, mutual respect for mission work, and enough grounded chemistry on both sides that this only fails if neither truly makes room for Spain and protected time.
reasons.drchatterjee: Rangan is second because the Barcelona coast walk and slow dinner delivered the strongest two-way conversation and emotional maturity on the list, but his explicit need for one clear main base makes the England-versus-Spain question a more serious long-term strain than with Joe.
reasons.dominiquecrenn: Dominique places third because even in a speed date there was real adult chemistry, depth, and mutual respect for purpose, but two intense public lives split between Barcelona and San Francisco would require a deliberately built relationship architecture from day one.
reasons.sahilbloom: Sahil is fourth because the values, integrity, and long-term seriousness are excellent for Pau, yet the interaction read more as disciplined mutual respect than warm emotional ease, and his side was notably less convinced about the practical fit.
reasons.thespacegal: Emily ranks fifth because there was genuine spark and teammate energy, but the continent-level logistics and lack of evidence that Spain could be a true anchor make the match feel more admirable than livable right now.
reasons.drjulie: Julie is sixth because her emotional intelligence and calm intentionality suit Pau well, but nothing in the speed date meaningfully proved she would enjoy, not just tolerate, the international rhythm and Spain-anchored life he actually lives.
reasons.poojadhingra: Pooja comes seventh because the warmth and groundedness were appealing and mutual, yet the Mumbai base, founder pace, and limited evidence of connection to Pau’s foundation world or international structure leave too much of the real partnership unanswered.
reasons.ankurwarikoo: Ankur is eighth because while the values and self-discipline are strong, the India-Spain distance plus a more systems-led than emotionally open impression make him the least convincing match for Pau’s need for softness, sustained presence, and easy mutual adaptation.

decision.note: Pau, my pick is Joe Wicks. He gave you the best combination of warmth, shared daily-life values, respect for your mission, and a date that actually felt easy in your body—not just good on paper—while still meeting you with substance and steadiness. Rangan is very close, but Joe feels more likely to protect the simple, grounded life you need if he’s truly willing to build around Spain.
